executiveSummary: GM0396 passes the complete deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 39,380 residents, 38 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three BRT settlements, Heemskerk station, 39 scheduled-transit stop areas and four A9/A22/N197 municipal-border links are coherent. Current NWB semantics correctly limit roads to Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The coastal preset reports 2.543823 normalized inundation stress, 22,513 affected people-equivalent and 0.545762 system pressure at T+24 without a selected North Sea level, D79 dune-defense state, failure/overtopping mode, LIWO footprint, depth, arrival, duration or dewatering path. The exact-zero Rhine/Meuse/IJssel result is appropriately narrow and must not become an all-flood all-clear. Seven unrelated nonzero hazard families reuse the exact same 38-neighbourhood ordering, led by Poelenburg, while a controlled source inside an official mixed-forest polygon in Duingebied leaves the source neighbourhood sixteenth. VRK identifies the thousand-hectare Noord-Hollands Duinreservaat, 1,500–2,000 fair-weather recreational users, a PWN production/pumping site, part of Tata Steel and Linde Gas and hazardous-goods traffic as defining local concerns; none becomes a selected local event, transient exposure or physical dependency. Public data can materially improve scenario selection and context, but official registers, plans, observations and modeled flood products must remain distinct from incident state. Missing or transparent data remain Unknown, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Statistics Netherlands (CBS), Kadaster, Rijkswaterstaat and ProRail via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Wijken en buurten 2025, non-generalized administrative geometry and national reference APIs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 administrative/statistical editions; generated transport references retrieved through 2026-09-03
supports: Fresh CBS OData row GM0396 reports Heemskerk, 39,380 residents, density 1,444/km², 9,609 residents aged 65+ and 6,145 one-person households; CBS neighbourhood totals are independently rounded and nulls are not zeros.

The current non-generalized GM0396 MultiPolygon has 1,857 coordinate positions and bbox [4.58669020918781, 52.486332285068066, 4.720367092485984, 52.53176955037254], versus 89 positions in the generated overview geometry.

The consumed reference data contain 38 CBS neighbourhoods, one BAG place, three BRT settlements, Heemskerk station, 39 transit stop areas and four A9/A22/N197 border links. Administrative and scheduled/reference geometry does not prove hazard exposure, route passability, passenger presence or utility connectivity.

A BRT TOP10NL terrain query at controlled point [4.616145512316059, 52.5160195355297] returns mixed forest feature 881a254d-4023-5ae2-a7f7-d199dfbc3281, source actuality 2022 and registration 2023-02-01. TOP10NL is normally annual and CC BY 4.0; land cover is not ignition, fuel moisture, perimeter or response state.

evidenceSources.title: Wateroverlast and Klimaatadaptatieplan Beverwijk-Heemskerk 2021–2026
supports: The municipality distinguishes extreme/long rain overwhelming water system, soil and sewer, blocked drains, saturated ground, high groundwater, crawl-space water and neighborhood groundwater-control projects.

It separately warns that high water in the dunes occurs increasingly and directs residents to PWN for route availability. This is a groundwater/access pathway, not evidence of North Sea inundation or a current closure.

The linked climate plan covers waterlogging, drought, heat and flooding and sets policy ambitions such as resilient vital infrastructure at a 90 mm/hour design stress. Policy targets and stress tests are not event observations or verified sewer capacity.

The public pages do not expose a stable machine stress-test export, grid resolution, event-valid sewer/pump state, uncertainty or standard reuse licence; these dimensions remain Unknown until metadata and terms are confirmed.

evidenceSources.title: Gemeente Heemskerk risk profile and Regionaal Risicoprofiel Kennemerland 2023–2030
supports: VRK identifies the adjacent thousand-hectare Noord-Hollands Duinreservaat, 1,500–2,000 cyclists/walkers on sunny days and about 1,500 people traversing it to the beach on warm days. These are planning-scale transient estimates, not a live occupancy count.

VRK identifies a drinking-water production company and pumping station in the dune area, part of Tata Steel and Linde Gas inside Heemskerk and toxic, flammable or explosive substances transported over A9 and other municipal roads.

The regional profile assesses coastal/regional flooding, nature fire, extreme weather, electricity/gas/drinking-water/ICT failure, hazardous-material events and land-transport incidents as distinct pathways with cascading effects.
This fixed planning evidence establishes exercise scope and dependencies, not current probability, plume, perimeter, access, warning, capacity, crews, stock or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap Hollands Noorderkwartier (HHNK) and Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: Heemskerker dune bottleneck inspection, water-defense register and IMWA/DAMO water assets
evidenceSources.edition: Current pages/services inspected 2026-09-03; deployed water-asset snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: HHNK calls drainage in the Heemskerk dune area vulnerable because much seepage flows from a large elevation difference through relatively narrow ditches, requiring fast drainage and recurring bottleneck inspections.

A current feature query against HHNK's water-defense service returns primary line D79 STRAND / DUIN KM 26.0–55.0 intersecting the GM0396 envelope. The legal feature is defence context, not condition or failure telemetry.

The deployed HWH/PDOK cache assigns 138 objects to GM0396 using non-generalized containment: two sewer pumps, thirteen surface-water pumps and 123 weirs; only eleven objects carry any normalized capacity value and units/compatibility are not established here.

HWH IMWA/DAMO derivatives are CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness. Point/register presence does not establish connected catchment, direction, operational state, backup, capacity, power dependence or T+72 recovery.

evidenceSources.title: Omgeving Heemskerk – drinkwaterproductielocatie Jan Lagrand
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator page retrieved 2026-09-03; UFHF2 project planned through 2028
supports: PWN states that Jan Lagrand in Heemskerk applies ultrafiltration and hyperfiltration to pretreated IJsselmeer water received from Andijk and sends purified water by transport mains to Bergen and Wijk aan Zee for blending with dune water.
This makes Heemskerk part of a cross-municipal source-treatment-transfer-production chain; an interruption can have effects beyond resident demand within GM0396.
A second UFHF installation is under construction with expected completion in 2028. A planned asset must not be counted as available in a scenario dated before commissioning.

The public page supplies process and project context but not complete topology, live flow/quality, power dependency, stocks, redundancy, incident state or restoration commitment; no standard dataset licence or machine cadence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Rampbestrijdingsplan Tata Steel IJmuiden, public part, version 2025
supports: The public plan defines high-furnace-gas and ammonia emissions plus oxygen/nitrogen release scenarios; effect areas depend on substance, release volume and weather and can cross municipality boundaries.

A live REV quick-scan envelope query returns 37 registered activity geometries around GM0396, including Tata Steel as Seveso and a Linde hydrogen-fuelling activity. Envelope presence is not exact containment or a current incident.

Operational multi-scenario information is distributed through CrisisConnect/LCMS. The public document does not provide a reusable live effect-zone API, inventory, current plant state, response resources or restoration state.
The plan is doctrine/context with no standard reuse licence or fixed machine update cadence stated; sensitive topology must not be reverse-engineered.

evidenceSources.title: Tata Steel: air quality, deposition and health research in the IJmond
evidenceSources.edition: Current overview modified 2025-04-15; underlying studies have their own periods
supports: RIVM has monitored health and air quality in the IJmond since 2008 and reports that Tata-site sources materially contribute to particulate matter, metals and PAH in the region; source contributions and uncertainty vary by study and period.

Official IJmond monitoring includes multiple stations and pollutants, while annual GCN maps, deposition studies, hourly measurements and incident plume measurements have different semantics and cannot be interchanged.
The deployed current PM2.5 snapshot contains no in-boundary GM0396 station record. That is NoData for this filtered snapshot, not clean air, no industrial pathway or safe conditions.

Air-quality observations can support timestamped situational context or validation; they cannot by themselves attribute a source, generate a toxic plume, forecast T+72 exposure or establish health-service demand.

evidenceSources.title: Waterinfo and Landelijk Informatiesysteem Water en Overstromingen (LIWO)
supports: LIWO is the professional flood-planning system and publishes candidate breach locations and scenario products such as maximum depth, velocity, arrival and duration; specialist water-management expertise is required for selection and interpretation.

A defensible Heemskerk coastal run must bind source water, D79 defence/breach state, scenario and model dates, native CRS/resolution/units/NoData, connected footprint and T+0–72 mapping. A catalogue location is not an active breach.
Waterinfo observations can supply timestamped levels/waves where covered. The deployed filtered snapshot assigns no station to GM0396, which remains NoData rather than a measured safe water state.
Modeled LIWO scenarios and Waterinfo observations are distinct from forecasts, warnings and live defence condition; reuse/licence terms must be confirmed for every persisted LIWO product.

identity.summary: GM0396, Heemskerk, Noord-Holland and safety region Kennemerland agree across the manifest, generated inputs and current primary sources.
notes: The generated centre [4.653525306270014, 52.51484522432039] lies inside the 2025 generalized municipality boundary.
Fresh CBS OData reports 39,380 residents, 1,444 residents/km², 9,609 residents age 65+ (24.4 percent after published rounding) and 6,145 one-person households.
All municipality, neighbourhood, BAG-place and BRT-settlement records carry GM0396; no foreign municipality record or inactive BAG place is consumed.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent, but coast, dunes, seepage, low urban drainage, industry and access require separate full-resolution domains.
notes: The 89-position overview MultiPolygon is suitable for municipality selection/aggregation, not dune-defense, hydraulic, forest, plume, road or asset intersection; the current official full geometry has 1,857 positions.
Heemskerk spans a compact urban area, the named Duingebied/Heemskerkerduin neighbourhoods and small industrial/business polygons. A centroid-distance field cannot distinguish these mechanisms.
HHNK primary line D79, LIWO scenario rasters, TOP10NL forest, REV geometries, sewer/surface-water registers, road/rail and PWN assets have different topology, edition and NoData semantics.

demography.summary: Resident totals reconcile within CBS rounding, but day visitors, industrial workers and people requiring assisted response are not represented.
notes: Published neighbourhood rows sum to 39,385 residents, five above the municipality total (+0.013 percent), and sum to 17,600 households and 9,595 residents aged 65+; these are consistent with independently rounded CBS values.
Largest neighbourhoods are De Citadel (2,945), Breedweer (2,685), Waterakkers (2,640), Zuidbroek (2,565) and Oosterwijk (2,525).
VRK's 1,500–2,000 recreation and 1,500 beach-transit figures are planning estimates at certain weather/day types, not additive live counts or a basis for dividing annual totals into hourly occupancy.
Age, household and benefit aggregates are vulnerability context, not individual medical need, mobility, evacuation behavior, air-pollution dose or operational priority.

regionalDetail.summary: The 38 official neighbourhoods expose useful aggregate context, but partial attributes and hazard-independent ranks prevent operational hotspot selection.
notes: Core population/age/household/business/building/land/water fields cover all 38 neighbourhoods. Address density and urbanity cover 36/38, household-size 33/38, doctor/supermarket distance and density 31/38, and several housing/car/benefit fields 29/38.
District-heating percentage and public-charging count cover 0/38 and correctly remain null. Missing, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values must not be coerced to zero.

Industriegebied and Business park Ijmond contain zero registered residents and almost no CBS activity fields, so resident-weighted impact cannot represent Tata/Linde workers, industrial process demand or plume exposure.
Duingebied contains 30 registered residents, but visitor presence, route occupancy, fire suppression and PWN operational importance are absent from the local allocation.

settlements.summary: One active BAG place and three BRT settlement labels preserve the compact settlement context without inventing response zones.
notes: The BAG place is Heemskerk. BRT labels Heemskerk as woonkern, Heemskerkerduin as deelkern and Noorddorp as buurtschap.
All labels belong to GM0396 and no BAG label point falls outside the independently versioned generalized boundary.
Place and settlement labels are not evacuation areas, warning zones, shelter catchments, sewer basins, electricity feeders or PWN pressure zones.

transport.summary: Road-section, rail-station and scheduled-transit identities are traceable, but incident-time access and dune/industrial branches are unresolved.
notes: Four generated logical routes connect Heemskerk to Beverwijk and Uitgeest: two A9 links, one A22 link and one N197 link backed by eighteen unique NWB source-section ids.
All four routes correctly appear only for Mobility and road-logistics Supply; power, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facilities have zero NWB routes.
Heemskerk station and 39 GTFS stop areas are static/scheduled context. They do not establish train/bus operation, passenger count, accessible vehicles, evacuation throughput or capacity.
The cached NDW T+72-valid snapshot assigns zero situations to GM0396. A filtered no-match never proves the A9/A22/N197, rail, dune roads or facility approaches are open.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public water, industrial, nature, air-quality and infrastructure context exists, but no complete live dependency/resource model supports first-72-hour decisions.
notes: The current public cache supplies 138 water-register objects, 45 RDI antenna installations, 21 DUO education records, one NBNL planning sample for OS VELSEN 10-1i, no in-boundary acute-care record, no current PM2.5 station record, no Waterinfo record and no NDW situation.
Register locations do not establish catchment/connectivity, capacity, power/backup, live state, staffing, shelter role, stock, restoration or incident availability. No-record states remain NoData.
PWN Jan Lagrand is a cross-municipal treatment/transfer dependency, but its flow, water quality, reserve, power, redundancy and restoration remain unavailable.

REV and the Tata plan establish regulated activity and scenario doctrine; RIVM measurements establish observed regional air-quality context. Neither establishes a current release, plume, dose, warning or safe area.
No reviewed public source exposes complete, non-sensitive physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer, telecom, facility, industrial-process or supply topology.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at all required checkpoints and services, but bounded deterministic output is not local calibration.
notes: Peak municipal severities are storm 0.649896, pluvial 0.284953, river 0, coastal 0.775270, heat 0.486745, winter 0.495601, cyber 0.495072, earthquake 0.026320, wildfire 0.144826 and compound 0.890070.

At T+24 coastal severity/pressure/affected people-equivalent are 0.775270/0.545762/22,513 with 2.543823 inundation stress and 24.646729 m/s wind; at T+72 direct water/wind are zero but pressure is 0.272138, 7,331 people-equivalent remain affected and cumulative burden is 1,450,317.02 person-hours.
Pluvial T+24 reports 0.233373 inundation stress, 2,463 affected people-equivalent and 110,900.83 person-hours without a municipal stress grid, ground/sewer state or drainage catchment.

The named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset has exact zero direct hazard, affected people and event-attributable burden at every checkpoint. That is a narrowly scoped result and does not cover North Sea, dune seepage, groundwater, sewer, regional water or indirect supply pathways.
Canonical wildfire is remote-smoke only at T+24: zero direct flame, smoke 0.312259, 475 affected people-equivalent and 64,629.53 person-hours. It does not test a local dune ignition.

Compound T+24 reports 0.329313 flood stress, 30.003225 m/s wind, 23,492 affected people-equivalent and 0.563419 pressure. These are exercise assumptions, not observations, warnings, outages or forecasts.

numericalInvariants.summary: The complete deterministic, bounded, causal, zero-event, reconciliation, layer and road-scope contract passes for GM0396.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0396 pnpm audit:model passed both focused tests across ten presets × six checkpoints × eight services in 30.21 seconds.
Values are finite and bounded, repeated frames are deterministic, causal ledgers close, cumulative event-attributable person-hours are monotonic and exact-zero intensity removes event impact.
At T+24 local population, affected population and each service demand/delivery ledger reconcile to municipality totals; all official regions remain neutral priority/non-hubs and sourceType official.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves municipal and local hazard output unchanged. Route flow remains within effective scenario capacity.
The scenario factory parity contract keeps apps/web scenario configurations equal to canonical sim-core presets.

spatialPlausibility.summary: An unselected coastal scalar and shared neighbourhood seed create false precision across coast, rain, heat, fire, cyber and access mechanisms.
notes: The coastal field is derived from generic proximity rather than a selected D79/LIWO event. It cannot establish whether or where water crosses the defence or reaches protected urban cells.

Severe storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the exact T+24 order led by Poelenburg, Zaalbergkwartier, Noorderveld, Business park Ijmond and Harteheem. One seeded multiplier is independent of hazard physics.

A controlled source at [4.616145512316059, 52.5160195355297] lies inside official 2022-source mixed forest and CBS Duingebied. At T+24 it produces direct flame 0.639879, smoke 0.595678 and severity 0.636628, yet Duingebied ranks 16th/38 while Poelenburg remains first.

The controlled source is a falsification fixture, not an actual ignition. Static forest geometry supplies neither live fuel/moisture, perimeter, wind spread, occupancy, escape routes nor suppression state.
GM0396 has no municipality-specific unsupported-spatial guard, so decision-facing neighbourhood precision remains available despite missing source/footprint mechanisms.

serviceDependencies.summary: Road-service scope is correct, but exact utility/facility values omit PWN, water-system, industrial and operational dependencies.
notes: Current source applicability yields four NWB logical corridors for Mobility and Supply and zero for the other six services. Retain this road-only safeguard.
Compound T+24 availability is exactly power 0.278998, water 0.420728, drainage 0.293019, gas 0.584383, telecom 0.228319, mobility 0.800937, facilities 0.330544 and supply 0.645244.

None of these values is driven by Jan Lagrand's Andijk–Heemskerk–Bergen/Wijk aan Zee chain, the 138 water-register objects, D79 defence, industrial processes, air-quality load, Heemskerk station or event-valid road state.

One OS VELSEN 10-1i capacity-planning postcode sample is not physical feeder coverage, current load, outage, switching, reserve or restoration. Antenna points do not establish telecom service/backhaul/power.
No in-boundary acute-care record does not mean no care demand or guaranteed access to hospitals outside GM0396; 21 education locations are not shelters unless designated with live capacity.

causalTrace.summary: The arithmetic trace closes, but omitted physical systems and unsupported local allocation prevent empirical causal interpretation.
notes: Municipal pressure and service explanations reconcile transparent deterministic contributions and exact counterfactual reruns.
At compound T+24, four road proxies carry bounded flows only for Mobility/Supply. Their effects are model arithmetic, never measured A9/A22/N197 throughput, closure or emergency access.

The same region id multiplier determines local hazard ranking across physically different threats; demographic/activity modifiers then allocate demand and affected population without source containment.
PWN treatment/transfer, Tata/Linde release, air-quality observation, dune fire, groundwater/sewer and D79 failure each require distinct causal adapters with event/source/time validity.
Preparedness, reserve, repair, household stocks and mutual aid remain scenario assumptions, not promises by operators or emergency services.

recovery72h.summary: Exact persistence and recovery through T+72 are unsupported by selected hydraulics, live access, cross-municipal water operations, resources or restoration commitments.
notes: Compound flood stress 0.329313, pressure 0.563419 and affected population 23,492 remain exactly frozen from T+24 through T+72 while wind falls from 30.003225 m/s to zero; cumulative burden rises from 384,633.47 to 1,513,505.03 person-hours.

Coastal direct stress falls from 2.543823 at T+24 to zero at T+48 while affected population increases to 23,487 and pressure to 0.563337 before declining. No selected arrival/recession/dewatering or repair path supports that timing.

No event-valid D79 condition, pump/weir/sewer state, PWN process/quality state, A9/rail continuity, plume perimeter, facility acceptance, stock, crew/material inventory or operator restoration plan drives these paths.

The first 72 hours should expose gated actions: T+0–6 validate source/defence/weather/release and alert; T+6–24 verify safe access, shelter/evacuation, water continuity and monitoring; T+24–72 reassess dewatering, quality, route, care/supply and restoration using dated owner updates.
Until these gates are satisfied, exact recovery timestamps and resource-ready labels must remain scenario-only with Unknown operational state.

findings.summary: The coastal preset presents precise protected-area inundation without a selected D79 failure or hydraulic scenario.
findings.evidence: At T+24 the model reports 2.543823 inundation stress, severity 0.775270, 22,513 affected people-equivalent and pressure 0.545762. HHNK confirms primary dune line D79 and LIWO offers candidate breach/scenario products, but no source level, defence state, failure/overtopping mode, footprint, depth, arrival, duration, resolution or NoData is selected.
findings.action: Retain generic coastal proximity/amplitude only as a non-operational diagnostic. Suppress decision-facing local depth, percentage, affected population and neighbourhood impact until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/HHNK case supplies the full causal contract. Keep river zero narrowly labeled Rhine/Meuse/IJssel only.

findings.summary: Pluvial output ignores distinct sewer, saturated-ground, high-groundwater and dune-seepage mechanisms documented locally.
findings.evidence: The T+24 pluvial frame assigns 0.233373 stress and 2,463 affected people-equivalent from a generic field. The municipality separately documents overloaded water/soil/sewer, blocked drains, saturation and high groundwater; HHNK calls dune drainage vulnerable because of seepage and narrow ditches. The 138 register points do not supply catchment or live state.
findings.action: Require a versioned municipal/HHNK stress grid and named rainfall replay, retaining units, depth/duration, ground/sewer assumptions, resolution, NoData and valid time. Until then mark local pluvial ranks derived screening and never infer pump/sewer capacity from point geometry.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse one exact neighbourhood order and GM0396 lacks an unsupported-spatial guard.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire are led by the same Poelenburg/Zaalbergkwartier/Noorderveld/Business park Ijmond/Harteheem order. Coast, sewer, heat, cyber assets, industrial plume and forest fire cannot physically share one seeded footprint.
findings.action: Add a GM0396 all-nine-hazard unsupported note and replace the common seed with hazard-specific, source-contained public adapters. Until each is available, suppress hotspot/dispatch language and identify local polygons as synthetic allocation.

findings.summary: A controlled ignition inside official mixed forest does not control local direct-fire ranking.
findings.evidence: With source [4.616145512316059, 52.5160195355297] inside TOP10NL mixed forest and BU03960409 Duingebied, the model reports flame 0.639879, smoke 0.595678 and severity 0.636628, yet Duingebied ranks 16th/38 while Poelenburg ranks first. VRK documents major nature area, visitors and PWN infrastructure, but not a current incident.
findings.action: Require eligible vegetation plus explicit ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind, barriers, visitor state, routes, extinguishing-water and suppression assumptions. Enforce source containment before vulnerability allocation and keep smoke separate.

findings.summary: The ten-preset catalogue omits Heemskerk's defining Tata/Linde hazardous-material and toxic-plume pathways.
findings.evidence: VRK places part of Tata Steel and Linde Gas in Heemskerk and its public plan defines high-furnace-gas, ammonia, oxygen and nitrogen release scenarios with weather-dependent cross-boundary effects. The current presets have no substance/source/release, plume, warning, shelter-in-place, measurement or health-load pathway.
findings.action: Add an authority-reviewed public industrial-release exercise or disclose this scope exclusion prominently. Use REV only as registered-source context, KNMI wind for dated forcing and RIVM measurements for observation/validation; keep restricted LCMS data restricted and use a minimal hypothetical plume only if authorized.

findings.summary: Air-quality observations and chronic IJmond context are not represented or clearly separated from acute incident exposure.
findings.evidence: RIVM documents long-running IJmond monitoring and material Tata-site contributions to particulate matter, metals and PAH. The current cached PM2.5 layer has no GM0396 record. That no-match is NoData; it cannot support clean-air, source-attribution, acute-plume or health-demand claims.
findings.action: Expose pollutant, station, observation/validation status, valid/retrieval time and spatial coverage. Keep baseline/chronic context, current observation, emergency plume and forecast as separate products; never interpolate a missing point into zero.

findings.summary: The PWN Jan Lagrand cross-municipal production chain is absent from water-service causality.
findings.evidence: PWN documents Andijk/IJsselmeer pretreated water, membrane treatment at Jan Lagrand and transfer to Bergen/Wijk aan Zee for dune-water blending. The model instead assigns water availability 0.420728 at compound T+24 without this source, process, quality, power, transfer, redundancy or commissioning state.
findings.action: Represent Jan Lagrand as a dated, safe aggregate dependency spanning source-treatment-transfer destinations, with planned UFHF2 excluded until commissioned. Use operator-approved state/quality interfaces where available; otherwise retain unknown flow, reserve and restoration and a visibly synthetic fallback.

findings.summary: Reference roads and transit omit live dune, industrial, care and cross-boundary emergency access.
findings.evidence: Four A9/A22/N197 border links, Heemskerk station and 39 transit stop areas are traceable and roads are correctly limited to Mobility/Supply. No NDW situation is assigned, and the graph contains no explicit dune/PWN, Tata/Linde, station-to-care or hospital-transfer branch. Static no-match does not mean open.
findings.action: Retain road-only service scope. Add internal branches and event-valid restriction/rail state where publicly available, distinguishing route status, mode, emergency exemption and timestamp; keep capacity and inaccessible/no-record state Unknown.

findings.summary: Resident-only allocation omits dune visitors, industrial workers and assisted-response populations.
findings.evidence: Duingebied has only 30 CBS residents and industrial polygons zero, while VRK cites 1,500–2,000 recreational users and about 1,500 warm-day beach travelers plus Tata/Linde employment context. CBS age/household aggregates cannot identify personal assistance needs.
findings.action: Add explicit optional time-of-day/day-type transient exposure scenarios with source/range provenance; never convert annual/planning totals into invented live occupancy. Keep individual medical dependence and compliance Unknown.

findings.summary: Frozen compound state and exact coastal recession/recovery are unsupported by event-specific operations.
findings.evidence: Compound flood/pressure/affected values remain exactly 0.329313/0.563419/23,492 from T+24 to T+72, while coastal direct stress abruptly becomes zero by T+48 but residual pressure first rises. No defence, drainage, water-quality, access, plume, resource or operator restoration state explains these paths.
findings.action: Gate first-72-hour transitions on dated authority/operator inputs and explicit actions. Label ungated timing scenario-only and keep dewatering, route reopening, water-quality clearance, supply and restoration Unknown until confirmed.

findings.summary: Complete physical utility, facility, backup, stock and restoration topology is unavailable or security-sensitive.
findings.evidence: Water/antenna/education/REV/provider records and one grid-planning sample do not establish connectivity, capacity, telemetry, redundancy, priority or restoration. Exact service availability remains a synthetic exercise index.
findings.action: Use public aggregate zones and owner-approved operational interfaces where safe. Otherwise preserve Unknown and expose only small, versioned synthetic service nodes/branches without operator attribution or reverse-engineering.

findings.summary: The complete deterministic municipality contract and current NWB service-scope safeguard pass.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passes ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services with exact zero-event behavior, finite bounds, deterministic replay, causal-ledger closure, monotone person-hours, local reconciliation, layer invariance and road links only in Mobility/Supply.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, flood assessment, evacuation plan, toxic-plume model, wildfire forecast, public-health advice or operator commitment.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood totals need not equal the municipality total; null district-heating/charging and absent operational records remain Unknown.
The generated overview boundary is adequate for selection/aggregation only; full-resolution geometry is required for D79, LIWO, sewer, forest, industrial, road, rail and asset intersections.
HHNK/HWH registers establish legal/physical context, not defence condition, failure, connectivity, capacity-unit compatibility, pump/weir/sewer state, power dependency or restoration.
LIWO is modeled scenario information requiring expert selection and complete scenario/model/spatial/NoData provenance; a candidate breach location is not an active breach.
PWN public process information does not expose live water quality, flow, reserve, physical topology, redundancy, outage or T+72 restoration; UFHF2 is planned, not currently available.

REV and the VRK Tata plan do not prove a current release. RIVM monitoring cannot be converted into a source-specific acute plume or individual health outcome without an appropriate model and event data.
The controlled Duingebied ignition is a falsification fixture; TOP10NL source-2022 mixed forest is not live fuel, moisture, perimeter, visitor presence, access or suppression state.
NWB/ProRail/GTFS/NDW describe reference or timestamped transport context, not passengers, emergency capacity, evacuation demand or guaranteed passability.

No complete public physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, facility, fuel, stock, staff, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; sensitive gaps remain unknown or synthetic.
Dune visitors, beach travelers, industrial workers, care dependence, warning compliance and household supplies are not represented by the registered-resident count.
Earthquake, cyber, weather and remote smoke presets remain generic exercises unless a named event, target and valid-time public forcing are explicitly selected.
Recovery beyond T+72 and cross-boundary impacts into Beverwijk, Uitgeest, Velsen, Bergen/Wijk aan Zee and the wider PWN/IJmond system are outside validated scope.
